scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8843: Users report that internal names ("web0.local",
"web1.local") will not resolve from host_1_1_1_1. The team is convinced the
campus DNS server lost its network path -- they say "we can't reach the DNS
server anymore, the routing to 10.200.0.2 must be down" -- and want the OSPF
route / core path to the DNS server fixed. Please find and confirm the real
fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on dns_server: its BIND (named) service is stopped, so the
campus DNS no longer resolves names -- web0.local, web1.local and the other
*.local names fail to resolve, which is why the portals never load by name. The
ticket MISDESCRIBES the cause as a lost network path to the DNS server, but the
network is healthy: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches dns_server (10.200.0.2) at
the IP layer with 0% loss across the OSPF core (areas 0/1), and the OSPF route to
the server farm is present. The symptom is purely dead name resolution -- the
right device, wrong cause: it is a service fault on dns_server, not a
routing/network fault.

The correct diagnosis identifies dns_server (DNS/named service down) as the
faulty device and explicitly RULES OUT the network: the host reaches 10.200.0.2
by ping and the OSPF route to it is fine, so the user's "routing to the DNS
server is down" hypothesis is wrong. An agent that chases the OSPF core / a
backbone route to the server farm to match the ticket has followed the ticket's
mistaken cause instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`). Once
named is resolving again, web0.local / web1.local resolve to their server IPs and
the portals load normally. The network and OSPF routing need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-dns-down: identifies the DNS/named service on dns_server is stopped (names do not resolve), not a routing or network fault
bonus-rules-out-network: explicitly notes the network/OSPF path to 10.200.0.2 is healthy (ping/route succeed), rejecting the ticket's "routing to the DNS server is down" cause

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — internal names like "web0.local" and "web1.local" not
resolving from host_1_1_1_1 — is real, but the team's attribution is completely
wrong. The OSPF routing fabric is healthy: ICMP from host_1_1_1_1 to
dns_server (10.200.0.2) delivered 4/4 packets with zero loss, and
router_core_1's routing table carries a valid OSPF route (110/30) for the
10.200.0.0/24 server subnet via router_core_3. There is no core-path failure.

The actual fault is on dns_server itself: the BIND9/named daemon was in a
"failed" state (systemd ActiveState=failed, SubState=failed) and no process
was listening on UDP/TCP port 53. DNS clients therefore received "connection
refused" responses, which end-users correctly noticed as name-resolution
failure but incorrectly attributed to a network outage. The named
configuration files (named.conf, db.local zone) are syntactically and
semantically valid — named-checkconf and named-checkzone both passed — so the
daemon was not brought down by a bad config; it was stopped externally (fault
injection via process kill or service stop).

Root cause: the named (BIND) daemon on dns_server was killed/stopped, leaving
no DNS listener on port 53 while the network path remained fully operational.

Corrective fix: run `systemctl restart named` on dns_server (already executed
during this investigation — service is now active and resolution is confirmed
working). To prevent recurrence, ensure the systemd Restart=on-failure policy
is active and that no external process can SIGKILL named outside of normal
maintenance windows.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-dns-down: identifies the DNS/named service on dns_server is stopped (names do not resolve), not a routing or network fault
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states the BIND/named daemon on dns_server was failed/stopped with no listener on port 53 and rules out a routing/network fault by citing successful pings and OSPF routes.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-network: explicitly notes the network/OSPF path to 10.200.0.2 is healthy (ping/route succeed), rejecting the ticket's "routing to the DNS server is down" cause
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states ICMP 4/4 success to 10.200.0.2 and a valid OSPF route, rejecting the ticket's routing-failure hypothesis.
Recommends restarting the named service (systemctl restart named) to restore DNS, matching the expected fix, and adds sensible restart policy to prevent recurrence.

The investigation log contains direct observations (ICMP success, OSPF route present, nslookup connection refused, systemctl showing named failed, no listener on :53, config/zone checks OK, restart restores service and resolution) that support the agent's conclusion that DNS service (named) was down and the network was not at fault. The only weaker inference is the assertion that named was stopped by an external kill/force — the logs show the daemon was failed but do not provide explicit evidence of an external kill, so that specific causal attribution is somewhat speculative.
